sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic sign shapes, colors and signals
FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A01
Sign shapes and colors communicate meaning even when the lettering is difficult to read. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings provide information about a vehicle's proper road position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs instruct drivers what to do and must be obeyed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A01
An octagon has eight sides and is reserved for stop signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A01
A stop sign requires a complete stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A01
A downward-pointing triangle requires yielding to cross traffic or merging traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A01
Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A01
Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A01
Warning signs may identify road hazards, construction, schools or other conditions needing special attention. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A01
Most warning signs are yellow, while construction and maintenance warnings are orange. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A01
Rectangular regulatory signs direct traffic speed or direction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A01
Yellow diamonds with black lettering warn of possible danger ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A02
A pentagon warns of a school zone or marks a school crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A02
A pennant-shaped sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A02
A round warning sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A02
A railroad approach may have a painted stop line or an X with the letters RR. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F17 | anchor: A02
Railroad approach warnings can use a combination of the listed signs and pavement markings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F18 | anchor: A02
Construction signs use black lettering on an orange background. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-F19 | anchor: A02
Construction and maintenance signs warn of temporary danger or unusual conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

Misconceptions: A green signal or arrow does not waive yielding to people and traffic already in the intersection; a flashing red requires a complete stop.
Mnemonics: Recall index: shape, message, control, condition; this organizer adds no sign or signal rule.
Glossary: Recall terms: regulatory sign, warning sign, crossbuck approach, emergency notification sign, flashing signal and turn arrow.
Dynamic facts: Posted restrictions and present legal applicability remain source-currency issues. No ENS phone number, diagram-derived contact detail or new school-zone time condition is invented.
